subject: Paragon Systems RFI: Admin role separation, SCIM mappings, and audit evidence
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paragonsys.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@paragonsys.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Paragon RFI - questions on admin roles, SCIM and audit logs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this RFI — Paragon is preparing a vendor short list for inference platform providers. We have a few focused questions on identity and access controls that are gating for the security review:

1) Admin role separation: please describe how Redwood models administrative roles. For each admin role we need to know default permissions, whether roles can be scoped by tenant/project, and whether you support least-privilege canaries (e.g., read-only vs full-admin).

2) SCIM provisioning: do you support role (Group) push via SCIM for automated onboarding? If so, what is the SCIM schema mapping for groups -> RBAC roles and how are conflicts handled on sync?

3) SSO/OIDC: we use Okta and Azure AD. Do you support both SAML and OIDC for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows? Any known limitations for provisioning attributes we should be aware of (email vs userPrincipalName mapping)?

4) Audit and separation: we need sample audit log artifacts showing admin activity (role assignments, policy changes, and token issuance). Please include retention policies and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM (we use Splunk).

5) Delegated admin & emergency access: is there a break-glass / just-in-time (JIT) admin flow and how is it recorded?

We attached an excerpt of the RFI (see initial_rfp_questions.pdf). If you can return a short matrix and a sample audit snippet by end of day Monday (Apr 13), that would help accelerate technical review.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Security Programs
Paragon Systems

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paragonsys.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Paragon RFI - questions on admin roles, SCIM and audit logs

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. High level responses inline, and I attached a role matrix (paragon_admin_role_matrix.csv) and our SCIM mapping (redwood_scim_mapping.yaml) for your team to review.

1) Admin role separation: Redwood ships with a small set of baked-in admin roles (Organization Admin, Security Admin, Deployment Admin, Billing Admin, Read-Only Auditor). All roles are tenant-scoped — you can constrain any role to a specific tenant or project. The attached CSV maps each role to capabilities (e.g., change-iam, modify-routing-policies, deploy-model). We also support custom role creation for least-privilege patterns.

2) SCIM provisioning: we support SCIM 2.0 with group-to-role mappings. The YAML shows the common mapping patterns we use (group.displayName -> role.name). Conflicts on sync (e.g., user in multiple groups mapped to overlapping roles) are resolved deterministically: we merge role grants and record the source group in the audit trail; teams can choose "deny overrides" or "allow merges" in the tenant sync policy.

3) SSO/OIDC: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC (both SP and IdP initiated). We have pre-built integrations for Okta and Azure AD and can accept custom attribute mappings — common gotcha is how different IdPs populate email vs upn; we include a mapping interface in the console plus API hooks for programmatic transforms.

4) Audit and separation: our audit pipeline records admin actions (role assignment, policy changes, token issuance, login events) with actor, timestamp, IP, and request context. Retention is configurable per-tenant (default 90 days), and logs can be forwarded to Splunk/Datadog/AWS S3 via our export connectors — sample snippet attached (audit_sample.log.txt).

5) Delegated admin & JIT: we offer an optional JIT access flow via time-limited elevation tokens. Elevations require an approver (configurable) and are fully logged. For high-risk ops we support required MFA and an approval step recorded in the audit event.

Next steps: Marissa, Ben — can you add any product-limit notes (rate limits for SCIM bulk-syncs, max group size, and any known IdP quirks)? Elena, happy to set a 30-min technical call early next week to walk the mappings.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paragonsys.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@paragonsys.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Paragon RFI - questions on admin roles, SCIM and audit logs

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments, that helps. A couple of clarifying points after a quick pass: 

- SCIM delta behavior: when a group is removed in the IdP, is the corresponding role revoked immediately or marked for manual reconciliation? We need to avoid orphaned privileges during rapid churn.

- Group to role mapping conflicts: can we set an explicit precedence rule (e.g., idp:engineering-group > idp:contractors) or is precedence purely alphabetical/deterministic?

- OIDC attributes: does Redwood accept nested claims (groups claim as array) during token exchange, or do you prefer SCIM for group syncs?

Also, please confirm whether Splunk export supports streaming ingestion (we'd like near real-time alerts for role escalations). If you can clarify these three points and paste a short audit sample showing a role revoke event, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@paragonsys.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Paragon RFI - questions on admin roles, SCIM and audit logs

Elena — looping in our product security lead, Kimberly, and Ben (solutions engineer) to ensure the answers are complete. Answers below and pasted a short audit sample for a role revoke.

- SCIM delta behavior: by default, inbound SCIM operations are applied immediately (adds/patch/removes). To avoid orphaned privileges during churn, many customers use our "grace window" policy where removals are staged for a configurable grace period (e.g., 24–72 hours) before the role is revoked; this is tenant-configurable. We record both the SCIM event and the resulting RBAC change in the audit stream.

- Precedence: you can define precedence rules per-tenant. The console supports an ordered precedence list and the API allows you to set explicit precedence (higher priority wins). If no custom precedence is configured, Redwood merges roles and marks any conflicting deny rules as "deny overrides" per policy.

- OIDC groups claim: we accept groups in OIDC tokens as an array and will honor group claims for on-login role attachments. However, for durable provisioning we recommend SCIM (group push) because it creates a persistent mapping in Redwood rather than ephemeral session-based grants.

- Splunk export: yes — our export connector supports near real-time streaming via HTTP Event Collector (HEC). Role escalations can be forwarded with sub-second delay to your SIEM depending on HEC config and network latency.

Sample audit snippet (audit_sample.log.txt attached):

2026-04-13T17:12:03Z | tenant=paragon | actor=svc-scim-sync@okta | event=role_revoke | target=user:elena.rossi@paragonsys.com | role=Deployment Admin | reason=group_removed 'paragon-deploy' | request_id=ab12cd34

If you'd like, Ben can run a quick SCIM sync demo during the call and we can show the grace-window behavior. Let me know preferred time windows for next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
